state.goal: Prevent duplicate SUNNY launches on an occupied loopback port while preserving unrelated processes.
state.observed: The lifecycle regression confirmed a fixture HTTP endpoint listening, but .NET GetActiveTcpListeners sometimes omitted that port. The launcher then started a second worker, which failed with EADDRINUSE; own cleanup ran. This repeated. Windows listener enumeration also omitted the known live SUNNY loopback app despite its process. Healthy expected HTTP probes remain the first reuse check.
state.acceptance: If a loopback port accepts TCP but lacks the expected HTTP identity, fail without launching or stopping anything. Keep startup serialized, bounded, and local.

questions.question: Which bounded occupancy guard should replace the demonstrated incomplete listener enumeration?

options.targeted_connect: Attempt a short TCP connect only to 127.0.0.1 and the requested port; an accepted connection or inconclusive timeout prevents launch, and connection refusal permits the serialized launch.
options.owner_enumeration: Use Windows Get-NetTCPConnection owner enumeration as the only occupancy check before launch.
options.preserve_enumeration: Keep .NET GetActiveTcpListeners as the only occupancy guard and rely on post-launch failure cleanup.
